claims.statement: Talon wires one `talon_mcp_middleware()` into the main `DeepAgentRuntime` and installs the same middleware in freshly compiled local subagents, so both paths receive the MCP adapter behavior.

Fresh local subagents receive only applicable approval rules and add `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware` when such rules exist; a precompiled runnable is refused whenever an active approval policy cannot be enforced inside it.

The CLI builds the model-backed runtime from MCP tools and callbacks, subagent/cron/checkpoint configuration, Talon MCP middleware, and an optional sandbox; it installs the persistent scheduler only when channels are configured and routes job execution and delivery through the host.

TalonHost starts the runtime before bound channels and scheduler, unwinds a failed partial startup, and on shutdown cancels work before stopping channels, scheduler, and runtime while continuing after component-stop failures.

`AgentRequest` carries host-supplied metadata and optional interaction handlers, while `AgentResult` carries acknowledged background IDs so the host can requeue results if it cannot deliver the reply.

DeepAgentRuntime builds a graph from Talon's filesystem, selected-model summarization and model selection, progress, approval, hook, task, background, skill, and supplied middleware; it removes skill-only MCP tools from the ordinary tool list and configures local subagents from the available catalog.

Each runtime invocation captures graph and approval snapshots under a tools lock; reload failure preserves the prior graph and replacement builds a graph before assignment, so an in-flight turn is not changed by a reload.
Runtime approval authority is disabled for cron and background-delivery requests, and invocation-scoped state is reset after execution.

Background subagents are in-memory, conversation-owned jobs with shared capacity; workers clear authorization and approval authority, safely convert failures and approval interrupts to bounded results, and restrict management to the owning conversation.

The host dispatches completed background results only for eligible conversations with exponential backoff and uses an unattended follow-up turn; acknowledged IDs are requeued when its reply was not delivered.
Cron delegation runs inline with a separate semaphore and timeout, forbids nested delegation, and returns a safe tool error on failure or timeout.

Model selection is scoped to an invocation: the runtime resolves an optional selected model, falls back to the default when it is unavailable, and its summarization middleware uses a cached summarizer sized for the selected model while subagents retain the startup summarizer.

Talon replaces the SDK task middleware with `TaskTools`, allowing only a named fresh local subagent to add unique catalog tool names to its configured tools for one task; it runs with fresh context rather than inherited parent history or skills.

Local task delegation may provide control messaging only for Talon-built local agents, whereas remote async subagents stream their configured graph with the task description and request cancellation on disconnect.

Talon loads hooks from a trusted assistant-home `hooks.json` for each invocation, rejects symlinked or non-regular files, excludes workspace hooks, and degrades unreadable or invalid content to an empty diagnostic snapshot so a turn may continue.

A Talon hook session validates hook-interrupt identity against its snapshot, thread, and prompt and caches fulfillment responses; a fresh local subagent derives an isolated child hook identity from the parent turn's snapshot and transcript runtime.
Hook denial suppresses the denied tool call, while hook allow does not bypass Talon's human approval policy for a protected call.

Focused hook tests cover wire event payloads, hook denial and approval interaction, tool failures, trusted-home loading, malformed and legacy configurations, per-turn reload, and child-subagent transcript isolation.

Talon replaces the SDK memory middleware with `TalonMemoryMiddleware`, which removes checkpointed memory contents before each turn so configured memory sources are reloaded without mutating the incoming checkpoint state.

The runtime's context doctor reads the active graph and a conversation checkpoint to produce a bounded, content-free context-cost report; it recomputes memory and skills without changing checkpoint state, and the host exposes it through `/context-doctor` without interrupting active work.

`deepagents-talon` 0.1.2 is an alpha Python 3.14 package that depends on Deep Agents, dcode, LangChain/LangGraph, and MCP; repository development resolves `deepagents` and `deepagents-code` as editable sibling sources.

Focused tests enforce transactional MCP and subagent graph reloads: failed compilation retains the prior graph/configuration, while an already-running turn completes on its original graph after a successful subagent reload.

Memory reload tests cover synchronous and asynchronous checkpointed turns, verify every configured memory source is refreshed after an edit, and verify a runtime sees a memory file changed through its filesystem tools on the next turn.

MCPToolProvider adds status, reload/configuration, and OAuth authentication tools around loaded MCP tools, serializes refreshes, and refuses management-tool name collisions; the runtime publishes refreshed tools only after it successfully builds their replacement graph.

Optional Claude Code and Codex session bridges are instantiated with the runtime's shared background delivery queue when their respective environment flags are enabled, while the optional dcode bridge is instantiated independently.

Claude Code and Codex bridges deliver only correlated, escaped responses to the originating conversation through BackgroundSubagents, while the dcode bridge sends a correlated prompt and accepts only an acknowledgement rather than a reply stream.

Session bridge tools deny non-operator turns and subagents. Their message tools are approval-protected by default when no policy entry exists, but an explicit unprotected policy disables the approval prompt without removing operator admission.

DeepAgentRuntime closes enabled Claude Code and Codex bridges before cancelling background workers; if worker cancellation does not complete, it leaves graph and checkpointer resources open rather than close them while a worker may still write.
